method: Both inputs are read in the browser and nothing is sent anywhere. For an interval whose just ratio is p:q, the upper pitch should sit at p/q times the lower one; the coincident partials are partial p of the lower pitch and partial q of the upper pitch, and the beat rate is their absolute difference. Cents are 1200 x log2(upper / (lower x p/q)), so a positive value means the upper pitch is sharp. Frequencies are accepted from 1 to 20,000 Hz; a pair more than 600 cents (half an octave) from the chosen ratio is refused as a likely entry error, and a beat rate above 25 per second is labelled too fast to count rather than tuned. The offset table recomputes the beat rate for -20 to +20 cents, and its rows load the corresponding upper frequency. Partials are assumed to be exact integer multiples: real strings are slightly inharmonic, piano tuning spreads octaves, and no decay or envelope is modelled.

sources.title: Beat (acoustics) - two partials a few hertz apart alternate between constructive and destructive interference, so loudness pulses at their difference frequency
Harmonic series - partial n of a tone sounds at n times its fundamental, so intervals are expressed as small integer ratios
Just intonation - the 1:1, 2:1, 3:2, 4:3, 5:4, 6:5, 5:3, 8:5 and 7:4 ratios used here
